title: Detached sessionization & enrichment stage for real-time console metrics
creator: Marco Li
description: Implement a detached enrichment stage that consumes raw console events, builds sessionized event streams per tenant, applies tenant metadata enrichment and transient aggregations, and emits a single enriched stream for downstream analytics, billing, and anomaly detection. The service must operate as a low-latency, horizontally scalable stream processor with deterministic replay capabilities and bounded in-memory state to avoid tail latency spikes.
motivation: Current ingest pipeline couples enrichment with the hotpath aggregator, making retries and reprocessing expensive and causing variability in tail latency. Splitting enrichment into a detached stage will allow independent scaling, easier replay, and quicker iteration on enrichment logic without risking hotpath stability.
design_summary: - Input: kafka topic console.raw.events (partitioned by tenantId). - Sessionization: sliding session window (30m inactivity threshold) computed with per-tenant clock skew tolerance. - Enrichment: attach tenant config, planId, quota buckets from tenant-lookup cache; flag experimental features. - Transient aggregation: compute ephemeral metrics (session length, event counts, first/last timestamps) kept in windowed RocksDB state with TTL. - Output: kafka topic console.enriched.events with schema v2 (adds sessionId, enrichedMetadata, aggregates). - Replay: support deterministic replay by storing processed offsets and ingesting from offsets; provide APIs to trigger reprocessing for a tenant-range. - Backpressure: use consumer group pause/resume and adapt parallelism per partition using dynamic workers. - Exactly-once: leverage Kafka idempotent producers and careful state checkpointing to avoid duplicates.
tradeoffs: - Choosing RocksDB for per-partition state increases disk usage but avoids cross-partition locking. - Sessionization threshold (30m) tuned to match UI sessions but may need per-tenant overrides. - Exactly-once via Kafka transactions adds latency in bursts; we mitigate via batching thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Enriched events produced with sessionId and tenant metadata for 99% of sample test traffic
Sub-100ms p50 additional latency introduced by enrichment on typical event sizes
Deterministic replay capability demonstrated for a 24h window on staging
Canary rollout completes without raising error rate above baseline on console-usage dashboard
Automated unit/integration tests cover session boundary cases and out-of-order event handling
notes: Initial prototype implemented in Go with sarama consumer, RocksDB state store, and protobuf schemas
We benchmarked memory/disk per-partition at ~120MB/partition with TTL=48h; need to validate for high-tenant cardinality
Tenant lookup cache implemented as LRU with async refresh from config-service; stale reads allowed for up to 60s
Will expose metrics: enrich_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), session_state_size_bytes, replay_lag_seconds, processed_events_total
